sub.title: Combat Superiority
sub.desc: Your experience on the battlefield has refined your fighting techniques. You learn maneuvers fueled by special dice called Superiority Dice. Maneuvers. You learn three maneuvers of your choice from the list below. Many maneuvers enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one maneuver per attack. You learn two additional maneuvers of your choice when you reach Fighter levels 7, 10, and 15. Each time you learn new maneuvers, you can also replace one maneuver you know with a different one. Superiority Dice. You have four Superiority Dice, which are d8s. A Superiority Die is expended when you use it. You regain all expended Superiority Dice when you finish a Short or Long Rest. You gain another Superiority Die at Fighter levels 7 (five dice) and 15 (six dice). Saving Throws. If a maneuver requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice) and Proficiency Bonus. Maneuver Options: Ambush. When you make a Dexterity (Stealth) check or an Initiative roll, you can expend one Superiority Die and add the die to the roll. Bait and Switch. When you're within 5 feet of a creature on your turn, you can expend one Superiority Die and switch places with that creature (if it's willing and not Incapacitated). Roll the die; until the start of your next turn, you or that creature gains a bonus to AC equal to the number rolled. Commander's Strike. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one attack to direct a willing ally who can see or hear you to strike. Expend one Superiority Die; that ally can immediately use its Reaction to make one attack, adding the Superiority Die to the damage roll. Commanding Presence. When you make a Charisma (Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion) check, you can expend one Superiority Die and add it to the roll. Disarming Attack. When you hit a creature with an attack roll, expend one Superiority Die to add it to the damage. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or drop one item of your choice that it's holding. Distracting Strike. When you hit a creature with an attack roll, expend one Superiority Die to add it to the damage. The next attack roll against the target by an attacker other than you has Advantage if the attack is made before the start of your next turn. Evasive Footwork. When you move, you can expend one Superiority Die, rolling it and adding the result to your AC until you stop moving. You can also Disengage as a Bonus Action. Feinting Attack. As a Bonus Action, expend one Superiority Die to feint, choosing one creature within 5 feet as your target. You have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature this turn. If the attack hits, add the Superiority Die to the damage. Goading Attack. When you hit a creature with an attack roll, expend one Superiority Die to add it to the damage. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have Disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of your next turn. Lunging Attack. When you make a melee attack on your turn, expend one Superiority Die to increase your reach for that attack by 5 feet. If the attack hits, add the Superiority Die to the damage. Maneuvering Attack. When you hit a creature with an attack roll, expend one Superiority Die to add it to the damage. Choose one willing ally; that creature can use its Reaction to move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the target of your attack. Menacing Attack. When you hit a creature with an attack roll, expend one Superiority Die to add it to the damage. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the start of your next turn. Parry. When a creature damages you with a melee attack roll, use your Reaction and expend one Superiority Die to reduce the damage by the number rolled plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier. Precision Attack. When your attack roll misses a creature, expend one Superiority Die and add it to the roll, potentially turning the miss into a hit. Pushing Attack. When you hit a creature with an attack roll, expend one Superiority Die to add it to the damage. If the target is Large or smaller, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 15 feet directly away from you. Rally. As a Bonus Action, expend one Superiority Die to bolster a willing ally within 30 feet that can see or hear you. That creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the Superiority Die roll plus half your Fighter level (round down). Riposte. When a creature misses you with a melee attack roll, use your Reaction and expend one Superiority Die to make one melee attack against the creature. If you hit, add the Superiority Die to the damage. Sweeping Attack. When you hit a creature with a melee attack roll, expend one Superiority Die to attempt to damage another creature. Choose another creature within 5 feet of the original target and within your reach. If the original attack roll would hit it, that second creature takes damage equal to the Superiority Die roll. Tactical Assessment. When you make an Intelligence (History or Investigation) check or a Wisdom (Insight) check, expend one Superiority Die and add it to the roll. Trip Attack. When you hit a creature with an attack roll, expend one Superiority Die to add it to the damage. If the target is Large or smaller, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have the Prone condition.

You learn a ritual that creates a magical bond between yourself and one weapon. The ritual takes 1 hour, which can be performed during a Short Rest. The bond fails if another Fighter is already bonded to the weapon or if it is a magic item attuned to someone else.

Once bonded, you can't be disarmed of that weapon unless you have the Incapacitated condition. If the weapon is on the same plane of existence, you can summon it to your hand as a Bonus Action.

You can have up to two bonded weapons, but can summon only one at a time with a Bonus Action. Bonding to a third weapon breaks the bond with one of the other two.
